Thanks for the template; filled with our best estimates (attached). TL;DR of what to assume for sizing:
- Model: prefer to serve a fine-tuned Llama-2-70B quantized (8-bit) for our highest-quality assistant; fallback to a 13B quant variant for cost-sensitive routes.
- Average tokens per request: input 120 tokens; output 260 tokens (average session ~380 tokens).
- Concurrency profile: steady-state 35 TPS, normal daily peak windows raise to 140 TPS (5–10 minutes at once) and an extreme marketing-driven burst we expect once per month where we hit ~360 TPS for ~3–7 minutes.
- SLA: interactive p95 target 200ms, p99 target 400ms. For the peak bursts, we can accept higher tail latency but need graceful degradation (fallback to 13B variant or queued bursts).
- Context window: typical active context 2k tokens; KV cache reuse across short sessions is high (~70%).

We attached our filled sheet (mosaic_token_profile.xlsx) — reach out if anything is unclear.

Thanks — I ran a quick sizing pass and attached the raw calc sheet (redwood_slab_calc_sheet.csv). Summary and key assumptions below. I focused on delivering a pragmatic committed slab + an operational burst strategy that balances cost and SLO fit.

Key runtime assumptions (our compiled runtime profile):
- Target production model: Llama-2-70B quant (8-bit) on H100-class instances using Redwood inference kernels. Measured median token throughput per GPU (steady interactive mix, 2k context, 70% KV reuse): ~28 tokens/sec. p99 latency margin assumed with our batching/autoscaling = +30% tail overhead under load.
- Fallback model: Llama-2-13B quant (8-bit) on same HW: ~145 tokens/sec per GPU (same context assumptions).
- Host-level batching and KV cache give effective token efficiency multiplier of ~1.35 during normal steady traffic (due to repeated prefixes from sessions).

Sizing outputs (rounded):
1) Committed slab to meet steady 35 TPS with 20% headroom:
   - Effective tokens/sec need = 35 * 1.2 = 42 TPS.
   - Using 28 tokens/sec per GPU effective -> 42 / 28 = 1.5 GPUs -> round up to 2 GPUs committed (H100).
   - Recommendation: commit 2 H100 GPUs for steady baseline (covers 35 TPS steady with headroom).

2) Day-to-day peak (140 TPS lasting 5–10 mins):
   - Effective required = 140 * 1.15 (peak burst inefficiencies) = 161 TPS.
   - With fallback mixing (we can steer some requests to 13B during the peak), effective blended tokens/sec per GPU: assume 60 tokens/sec per GPU blended across cluster.
   - GPUs needed = 161 / 60 ≈ 2.7 -> round to 3 GPUs additional as burst pool.
   - Recommendation: set burst slab of 3 GPUs (on-demand reserved burst or short-term capacity) that can be enabled during daily peaks.

3) Monthly extreme burst (360 TPS for 3–7 minutes):
   Options evaluated:
    A) Provision permanent extra slab (costly): 360 -> effective 360*1.2=432 -> at 28 tps/GPU = 15.4 -> ~16 GPUs (not ideal).
    B) Overflow to Redwood hosted pool for short minute-level spikes (fast routing + envelope limits) and enable fallback to 13B for non-critical routes.
    C) Hybrid: short-term slab reserve (pre-warmed) of 6 GPUs + overflow to hosted for remainder.
   - Recommendation: Hybrid (C). Pre-warm 6 GPUs (reduces hosted overflow and keeps a large portion of requests on 70B), route lower-priority traffic to 13B fallback and send the remainder to Redwood hosted transient capacity. This keeps cost bounded while preserving quality for priority traffic.

4) KV cache / context notes:
   - High KV reuse (70%) materially improves effective throughput — we've folded that into the 28 tps/GPU number. If reuse drops below 40%, expect per-GPU tokens/sec to fall by ~20–30% depending on prompt variance.
   - If contexts grow above 4k, memory pressure will reduce batching headroom; we should add an additional GPU for every ~50% increase in average context size beyond 2k.

Latency / SLO fit:
- With the recommended committed slab (2 GPUs) + 3 GPU burst pool we should meet p95 200ms in steady conditions. p99 at peak will depend on routing/fallback: with the blended strategy p99 should stay near 400ms for priority traffic. The monthly 360 TPS spike will likely push p99 above 400ms unless we pre-warm GPUs; hybrid pre-warm recommended.

Open risks / asks:
- Need confirmation which routes MUST stay on 70B (priority) vs routes that can accept 13B fallback.
- Confirm if Mosaic needs encryption-in-use/HSM constraints for private deployment; that changes instance types and memory profiles.

I attached the calc sheet and can pull a short PDF with the numbers for the customer.

Marissa

Subject: Redwood proposal: Mosaic dedicated slab recommendation + next steps

Hi Erin —

Thanks for the profile and Marissa's fast sizing pass. Attached is a short proposal PDF that summarizes the recommended committed slab, burst strategy, and the operational playbook for monthly spikes (mosaic_redwood_proposal_v1.pdf). Highlights below: 

Proposal highlights:
- Commit: 2 H100 GPUs (steady baseline) to cover 35 TPS with 20% headroom.
- Burst: 3-GPU burst slab to cover daily peaks to ~140 TPS (enabled via autoscale policy).
- Monthly spikes: Hybrid approach — pre-warm 6 GPUs for the spike window + overflow routing to Redwood hosted pool; prioritization rules keep premium traffic on 70B and steer cost-sensitive calls to 13B fallback.
- SLOs: With this configuration and the routing rules we expect p95 <= 220ms steady and p99 ~350–420ms depending on burst mix. We will instrument cost & quality monitoring and set automated fallback thresholds to protect SLOs.
- Next steps: 1) Mosaic to flag priority routes that must stay on 70B, 2) confirm commit term (12/24 months) and burst billing model, 3) schedule a 30-minute ops review to run through pre-warm timing and failover wiring.

I linked a draft Drive folder with the calc sheet and the proposal. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow morning PT to walk the numbers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
